title: Power Automate: view property values inline on cards in the new cloud flow designer
summary: The layout-control path starts inside the designer without explaining how to reach it from Power Automate. The feature description and licensing are supported, but the briefing should also acknowledge an archived release-plan excerpt that gives a different default and target month.

claims.claim: This feature belongs to Power Automate.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The feature is a capability of the new cloud flow designer.
claims.quote: Power Automate: Cloud flows - View property value expanded inline in new cloud flow designer

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The inline view displays property values at design time directly on action cards.
claims.quote: When you add an action, you can view property values for multiple steps at design time, or output values for multiple steps at runtime. The inline view shows this information directly on the cards

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment

claims.where: summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Without inline view, makers open each card individually to see values already accessible in the side pane, one step at a time.
claims.quote: Without the inline view, you select each card individually to see its value in the side pane, and you can view only one step's value at a time.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: The side pane remains the default and makers choose the inline view, represented as user-opt-in.
claims.quote: You can choose which experience you prefer. The current side pane experience remains the default. You can switch to the inline view whenever you want and switch back at any time.
claims.fix: Keep user-opt-in and the roadmap's side-pane default. Add to What's changing: "An archived release-plan excerpt indexed by Microsoft Learn describes inline display as the default and gives February 2026 as its general-availability target; this briefing follows the current roadmap record's side-pane default and June CY2026 target." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/release-plan/2025wave2/power-automate/view-property-value-expanded-inline-new-cloud-designer. The excerpt says "The feature shows all that information inline by default" and "Feb 2026"; fetching its URL redirects to an overview marked archived as of October 2026.

claims.claim: The cited designer page does not identify Layout as the roadmap's inline property-value and runtime-output view.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Power Automate maker path to the layout control is Cloud flows designer > Collapse (configuration pane) > Layout.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane to the left, select My flows. In the Cloud flows tab, select the flow you want to open. On the command bar at the top, select Edit. The flow opens in the designer.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui.path and the rendered path with "My flows > Cloud flows > flow > Edit > New designer (on) > Collapse (configuration pane) > Layout". Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/data-operations to sources for the route into the designer. Keep https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/flows-designer as docs: it documents the New designer toggle, Collapse button and Layout control. The current path starts inside the designer rather than at the maker portal's navigation.
